    10  
    11  /-!
    12  # Well-founded relations
    13  
    14  A relation is well-founded if it can be used for induction: for each `x`, `(∀ y, r y x → P y) → P x`
    15  implies `P x`. Well-founded relations can be used for induction and recursion, including
    16  construction of fixed points in the space of dependent functions `Π x : α, β x`.
    17  
    18  The predicate `WellFounded` is defined in the core library. In this file we prove some extra lemmas
    19  and provide a few new definitions: `WellFounded.min`, `WellFounded.sup`, and `WellFounded.succ`,
    20  and an induction principle `WellFounded.induction_bot`.
    21  -/
    22  
    23  @[expose] public section
    24  
    25  theorem acc_def {α} {r : α → α → Prop} {a : α} : Acc r a ↔ ∀ b, r b a → Acc r b where
    26    mp h := h.rec fun _ h _ ↦ h
    27    mpr := .intro a
    28  
    29  theorem exists_not_acc_lt_of_not_acc {α} {a : α} {r} (h : ¬Acc r a) : ∃ b, ¬Acc r b ∧ r b a := by
    30    rw [acc_def] at h
    31    push Not at h
    32    simpa only [and_comm]
    33  
    34  theorem not_acc_iff_exists_descending_chain {α} {r : α → α → Prop} {x : α} :
    35      ¬Acc r x ↔ ∃ f : ℕ → α, f 0 = x ∧ ∀ n, r (f (n + 1)) (f n) where
    36    mp hx := let f : ℕ → {a : α // ¬Acc r a} :=
    37        Nat.rec ⟨x, hx⟩ fun _ a ↦ ⟨_, (exists_not_acc_lt_of_not_acc a.2).choose_spec.1⟩
    38      ⟨(f · |>.1), rfl, fun n ↦ (exists_not_acc_lt_of_not_acc (f n).2).choose_spec.2⟩
    39    mpr h acc := acc.rec
    40      (fun _x _ ih ⟨f, hf⟩ ↦ ih (f 1) (hf.1 ▸ hf.2 0) ⟨(f <| · + 1), rfl, fun _ ↦ hf.2 _⟩) h
    41  
    42  theorem acc_iff_isEmpty_descending_chain {α} {r : α → α → Prop} {x : α} :
    43      Acc r x ↔ IsEmpty { f : ℕ → α // f 0 = x ∧ ∀ n, r (f (n + 1)) (f n) } := by
    44    contrapose!
    45    rw [nonempty_subtype]
    46    exact not_acc_iff_exists_descending_chain
    47  
    48  /-- A relation is well-founded iff it doesn't have any infinite descending chain.
    49  
    50  See `RelEmbedding.wellFounded_iff_isEmpty` for a version in terms of relation embeddings. -/
